variants.headline: Party divides in two
variants.sub: A split in {party} has produced the new party {splinter}.
variants.body:
The party {party} has split, with {splinter} the new breakaway party. The division is an organisational fact, not a complete explanation of the differences behind it. In considering {target}, readers should distinguish the break itself from unreported motives, ideological labels or claims about the balance of parliamentary strength.

A party has split in two. A simple sentence for a very public break. There is no need to invent the private quarrel to make it interesting. Readers should ask what the division is for, and whether the people being represented will find something more useful than competing claims to loyalty.

We judge {target} harshly in this matter. Political organisation carries obligations beyond the comfort of its leaders, and division is an appropriate occasion to question the quality of that stewardship. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
